subject: render warnings: "You must not set both chunk options out.width and fig.retina"?

messages.author: c2a4124666613378
messages.subject: render warnings: "You must not set both chunk options out.width and fig.retina"?
parts:
Hello,

This is not critical, but I've been getting a number of warnings recently when using Nvim-R to render Rmd to HTML (\kh).

For example:

    In addition: Warning messages:                                                                                                                                               
    1: In fix_options(params) :                                                                                                                                                  
      You must not set both chunk options out.width and fig.retina                                                                                                               
    Calls: nvim.interlace.rmd ... process_group -> process_group.block -> call_block -> fix_op...

I sometimes set the 'out.width' parameter for a chunk to control the figure size, so it seems to have a conflict with this.

Any suggestions?
Keith

messages.author: b256a2742aacd200
messages.subject: Re: render warnings: "You must not set both chunk options out.width and fig.retina"?
parts:
Can you please apply the attached patch to https://github.com/jalvesaq/R-Vim-runtime ?
It highlights the simultaneous occurrence of both out.width and fig.retina as an error.
What do think about this solution?

messages.author: b256a2742aacd200
messages.subject: Re: render warnings: "You must not set both chunk options out.width and fig.retina"?
parts:
Note: To apply the patch, do:

cd R-Vim-runtime
patch -p1 < fix_retina.patch

parts:
Hi Jackson,

I'm not actually setting 'fig.retina' anywhere in my analyses, so highlighting the conflicts won't happen in this case.

I originally thought that it might be something that would being added by NVim-R, but I tried rendering the document outside of vim now, and the warnings still appear.

I will follow up with rmarkdown and see what is going on.

Thanks for the help!
Keith
